title: Product PRD & Roadmap: Unified Inference v7
author: Asha Patel
content:
Overview

Summary:
Redwood Unified Inference v7 is the next major product release focused on improving inference economics and reliability for mixed workloads across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments. v7 synthesizes runtime kernel advances, smarter routing policies, and a simplified pricing tier that better aligns with customer latency and cost objectives.

This document contains: product requirements (PRD), high-level design specs, roadmap and themes for the next three quarters, pricing & packaging updates, and release notes for the public launch.

Goals and success metrics:
- Reduce median tail latency (p95) for batched text-generation workloads by 15% on common model families (LLaMA2-13B, Mistral) vs v6.
- Reduce per-token cost for mixed chat + embeddings workloads by 12% via improved batching, KV cache sharing, and a new caching policy.
- Enable predictive rollouts for Dedicated/Private customers with A/B traffic split and automatic fallback.
- Achieve >= 99.95% availability for hosted API endpoints at GA.

Primary customers and use-cases:
- PLG developer teams who need consistent latency across dev->prod.
- Platform teams standardizing inference across business units.
- Regulated customers deploying to Private with predictable cost and auditability.

Ownership:
- Product lead: Asha Patel
- Eng lead (serving runtime): Daniel Kim
- Eng lead (platform/console): Marina Lopez
- SRE/ops: Owen Zhang

Requirements (PRD)

1) Functional requirements
- FR-1: Unified API parity: All existing text generation, chat, embeddings, and function-calling endpoints must be supported without breaking changes.
- FR-2: Model variants: Support automatic routing between high-accuracy and low-cost quantized variants with latency and cost-aware policies.
- FR-3: Predictive rollouts: Canary/A-B rollout controls exposed in Console with traffic percent, metrics guardrails (latency, error-rate, unit-cost), and automatic rollback.
- FR-4: Improved caching: Implement prefix-KV sharing across concurrent sessions for identical prompts and enable time-windowed cache sharing for privacy-aware groups.
- FR-5: Private deployment parity: The Private control plane must expose the same rollout and model variant controls via the operator API.

2) Non-functional requirements
- NFR-1 (SLOs): Hosted endpoints must meet 99.95% availability and p95 latency targets per model family described in Performance Targets table below.
- NFR-2 (Performance): Per-token CPU/GPU utilization must improve by at least 8% for small-to-medium sequence lengths (<= 512 tokens) vs baseline.
- NFR-3 (Scalability): System must support autoscaling to 10k concurrent connections for multi-tenant hosted clusters.
- NFR-4 (Security): All customer data-at-rest and transit must comply with existing KMS/HSM policies and audit logs preserved for 90 days (configurable).

Performance Targets (examples):
| Model family | p50 latency (ms) | p95 latency (ms) | tokens/sec per GPU |
|--------------|------------------:|------------------:|-------------------:|
| LLaMA2-13B   | 45               | 220               | 3500               |
| Mistral-7B   | 30               | 150               | 4800               |
| GPT-like 70B | 180              | 900               | 700                |

Design specifications (high level)

Architecture changes:
- Kernel selection: Extend the compilation layer to pick between four kernel profiles (low-memory, low-latency, throughput-optimized, quantized-fast) at request time based on model, sequence-length hint, and current GPU load.
- Smart router enhancements: Introduce route scoring that incorporates dynamic cost-per-token estimates and cold-cache penalty. Router exposes an API to retrieve expected unit-cost and estimated latency for a candidate route.
- Cache-sharing policy: New 'grouped-kv' cache mode that permits short-lived KV sharing for identical prefixes across sessions within the same tenant and privacy label. Mode is off by default for public tenants, opt-in for dedicated/private.

APIs and Console UX:
- Console: rollout wizard with three steps: 1) Select model variant & traffic %, 2) Choose guardrails (latency threshold, error-rate, unit-cost delta), 3) Start rollout. Includes realtime charts and automatic rollback toggle.
- REST API additions:
  - POST /v1/rollouts -> body: {"service_id","model_variant","traffic_split","guardrails":{...}}
  - GET /v1/routes/estimate?model=...&seq_hint=... -> returns estimated latency & cost (JSON).

Security and privacy considerations:
- Grouped-KV cache includes TTLs and access-labels. Cache sharing requires explicit tenant config and audit logging on any shared retrieval.
- Private deployments log cache metrics locally; no cross-customer cache sharing.

Implementation milestones (epics)
- EPIC-1: Kernel selection & runtime glue (eng-serving-runtime) — 6 weeks
- EPIC-2: Router scoring & cost estimation API (eng-platform) — 4 weeks
- EPIC-3: Grouped-KV cache mode + tests (eng-serving-runtime + eng-sre) — 5 weeks
- EPIC-4: Console rollout UX + API integrations (eng-platform + product) — 4 weeks
- EPIC-5: Private control plane parity & docs (eng-private-deployments + security) — 6 weeks

Roadmap and themes (Q3-Q4 2026)

Themes:
- Theme A: Economics first — model/quantization recommendations, batch-tuning presets, and new pricing alignment for v7.
- Theme B: Predictable operations — canary tooling, rollback automation, and expanded observability.
- Theme C: Private parity — ensure feature parity and operator UX for on-prem/VPC deployments.

Quarterly roadmap (high-level):
- Q3 2026 (Jul-Sep): EPIC-1 + EPIC-2 complete; internal beta for hosted customers; early access to Dedicated customers. Begin billing integration for new pricing tiers.
- Q4 2026 (Oct-Dec): EPIC-3 + EPIC-4 complete; GA launch for hosted API v7; Console rollout GA; Dedicated generally available. Private parity work continues with partner pilot customers.
- Q1 2027 (Jan-Mar): EPIC-5 complete; Private GA; iterative tuning and quality/regression monitoring.

Pricing & packaging notes (summary)

Rationale:
Customers told us they prefer clearer cost predictability when mixing chat (low latency) and embeddings (throughput). v7 pricing simplifies tiers and introduces a new "Predictable" tier for workloads that need committed performance.

Proposed pricing changes (effective at GA):
- On-demand (existing): unchanged base per-token rates but improved discounting on long-request durations using 'burst credits'.
- Predictable tier (new): monthly commitment model for Dedicated/Hosted Predictable customers with guaranteed p95 latency SLOs and lower unit costs. Commitments: 1/3/12 month terms with escalating discounts.
- Private licensing: flat platform fee + per-GPU seat; optional managed support add-ons.

Sample packaging matrix:
| Package | Included | SLA | Price indicator |
|---------|----------|-----|----------------:|
| On-demand | Hosted API, pay-as-you-go | Standard (99.9%) | $ (baseline) |
| Predictable | Committed units, priority routing | 99.95% | $$ (lower unit cost) |
| Dedicated | Reserved GPU pools | 99.95%+ | $$$ (contract) |
| Private | Operator control plane, on-prem option | By contract | $$$$ |

Billing impacts & tracking:
- Add unit-cost estimation in Router API to show customers expected monthly spend for a given traffic split.
- Console cost-reporting will add a per-rollout cost impact preview.

Migration notes (for existing customers):
1. Default behavior: existing customers stay on current billing/pricing unless they opt into Predictable.
2. Migration tool: Console flow to estimate savings and projected SLO outcomes when switching to Predictable or Quantized-variant routes.

Release notes (v7 GA)

Release date: 2026-10-12 (planned)

Highlights:
- New kernel selection paths delivering 10-20% median latency improvements for common workloads.
- Smart router cost estimates exposed via API and Console.
- Console rollout wizard with automated guardrail-based rollback.
- Grouped-KV cache mode (opt-in) for dedicated/private tenants enabling higher effective cache-hit rates for multi-session applications.
- Predictable pricing tier announced with early-bird commitments.

Breaking changes and migration guidance:
- There are no breaking public API changes. Internal route scoring fields are additive.
- For customers relying on previous cache isolation semantics: grouped-KV is opt-in; default remains previous cache behavior.

Known limitations at GA:
- Grouped-KV mode is initially unavailable for public on-demand tenants and requires tenant opt-in.
- Router estimation is heuristic-based; we will iterate the estimator in the first two quarters post-GA.

Operational playbook (summary steps for GA rollout)
1. Internal canary: deploy v7 to 5% internal-only traffic on staging clusters for 2 weeks. Monitor p95, error-rate, GPU OOMs.
2. Beta customers: onboard 10 early customers across PLG and Dedicated. Run migration tool and collect feedback.
3. Gradual ramp: 10% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100% over 4 weeks with automatic rollback thresholds on latency (+30% p95) and error-rate (+0.5% absolute).
4. Post-GA: maintain weekly health checks for first 90 days.

Telemetry and metrics to monitor:
- p50/p95 latency per model family, per region
- effective unit-cost per token (estimated) per tenant
- cache hit rate (grouped-kv vs baseline)
- rollout-related rollbacks and guardrail triggers

Open decisions (ADR candidates)
- ADR-101: Default cache-sharing TTL (30s vs 120s) for grouped-kv. (targeted decider: eng-serving-runtime + privacy).
- ADR-102: Pricing discount bands for Predictable tier (exact percent tiers). (targeted decider: product + finance).

Appendices

  "service_id": "svc-12345",

}
